messages:
Elaine K: Quick heads-up — Cobalt asked to run a focused perf/W + kernel-tuning sweep next Tue/Wed. They want watt vs throughput curves across batch sizes and two quant profiles. Primary ask: clear telemetry and a reproducible kernel flags matrix.

Mike L: ok. I'll own telemetry and the run harness. need to confirm which power counters they want (nvml + RAPL?) and if they can share out-of-band power logs. :eyes:

Sam W: RAPL + NVML is fine. also let's capture L3/cache hits and cpu_cpi PMU. add timestamps to align samples.

Anya P: For kernel flags, recommend we test three sets: default, prefetch=on+noprefetch=0, and our latency-tuned set (noprefetch=1 cpufreq=tuned). I'll paste a quick config.

Mike L: thanks. draft harness command below — feel free to copy.

Mike L: ```bash
./bench-run --model electra-13b --batch 1,2,4,8 --seq 512 --quant qp8,q4_0 
  --kernel-flags "prefetch=on;latency_mode=1" 
  --telemetry nvml,rapl,pcm --telemetry-interval 100 
  --out s3://redwood-partner-bench/cobalt/<run-id>/ 
  --meta tags="cobalt,partner-sweep,round3"
```

Elaine K: perfect. can we also export per-step token timings and kv-cache hit ratio? Cobalt wants those plotted against watts.

Leo M: we can add kv-cache metrics. We'll emit a compact CSV and a jsonl trace for each container. Example fields: ts, step, tokens_generated, p50_latency_ms, watt_avg, kv_hit_ratio.

Sam W: need to define success criteria: throughput drop <10% when enabling latency-tuned kernel vs default at same watt level? or we publish full curves and let partner annotate.

Anya P: publish full curves + highlight the kernel delta. agree on a small summary metric: delta_Throughput@75W.

Elaine K: schedule — Cobalt prefers Wed for a live review. Mike, can you provision the runs Monday so we have data by Tue EOD?

Mike L: provisioning Monday AM. I'll spin 6 nodes with mixed batch sizes; bench-bot will kick off runs.

bench-bot: scheduled 6 jobs for run-id cobalt-20260418-01, starts 2026-04-20T09:00Z. Posting live logs to https://bench.redwood.internal/cobalt-20260418-01

Leo M: dashboard template created: /dashboards/partner/cobalt-watt-throughput. It has watts vs throughput, kernel-toggle overlay, and kv-hit heatmap. I gave view access to @elaine @mike @sam.

Mike L: FYI — we'll keep one control node with vendor kernel, others with our tuned kernel. ensure we pin bios p-states to avoid noise.

Sam W: noted. also capture ambient temp from datacenter probe so we can normalize perf/W.

Elaine K: thanks team. action items: Mike (provision + run harness), Leo (dashboard & CSV schema), Anya (kernel matrix + flags list), Sam (success metric + PMU list). I'll draft the joint comms doc for the post-run sync with Cobalt.

Anya P: putting kernel flags matrix into the run repo now -> s3://redwood-partner-bench/cobalt/kernels/flags-v3.yaml

Mike L: provisioning done. bench-bot kicked jobs. will update thread with first result snapshot. :rocket:

bench-bot: job cobalt-20260418-01/3 finished. sample: throughput=12.3 seq/s, watt_avg=78.6W, kv_hit=0.92. results uploaded to s3://redwood-partner-bench/cobalt/cobalt-20260418-01/results.jsonl

Sam W: initial look — tuned kernel improved p50 by 8% at the same watt band, throughput curve shifts right. will run statistical check and post summary.

Elaine K: excellent. planning slot with Cobalt for Wed 16:00 UTC to review. I'll send calendar invite and include run artifacts. :calendar:

Mike L: adding run artifacts link to the invite. thanks all.

Leo M: leaving a tiny note — for publishable graphs, we should smooth 5-sample windows and include shaded CI. will add to dashboard template.

Sam W: +1 on CI. Also let's capture kernel dmesg and perf-map for failed runs.

Elaine K: copy. we'll aim to have the public-facing joint report ready within 3 business days after the review.

Mike L: ack.
